- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 14-day moving avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then apply mean reversion toward 14-day MA.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.15) over 3+ days, model tends to overestimate — apply downward bias of 2–5% per day of sustained positive sentiment.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.0–0.15) — increase forecast by 3–7% if recent 7-day MA is below 70.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–14 days, model still holds upward bias — adjust downward by 1–3% per day of lagged sentiment negativity.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.3, -0.28, -0.33), model tends to ignore them — reduce forecast by 5–8% for each negative sentiment event within last 7 days.
